headline: Genomic comparisons trace duplication, selection, and incompatibility in animals
label: Comparative Evolutionary Genomics
summary: Expanded genome and transcriptome sampling now resolves how toxin, receptor, and immune gene repertoires diversified across metazoan lineages.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how gene repertoires and genomic barriers evolve across animal lineages, using comparative sequence data from populations to phyla. Spider ICK toxin analysis, built on a new Hadronyche cerberea genome and 86 transcriptomes, indicates ancient bivalency arising via intra-exonic duplication. A comparative study of 2,843 IAP proteins from 312 metazoan species reports lineage-specific duplication and loss. In ants, analysis of 55,068 odorant receptors across 163 genomes links positive selection on 9-exon ORs to social organization. A cross-phylum single-cell atlas of circulating immune cells from nine bilaterians identifies conserved MiT/TFE-driven phagocytic programs. The Formica study addresses a related question at the population level, mapping persistent genomic incompatibilities under speciation with gene flow. Together these studies pair broad taxonomic sampling with explicit tests of selection, duplication, and incompatibility.
